The Problem
02
Human Inspection Failures
Manual visual inspection is still the industry standard. Inspector 
fatigue, inconsistent hangar lighting, and subjective judgment 
lead to missed defects. Aviation safety bodies consistently cite 
human error during MRO as a top contributor to aircraft 
incidents.
Cloud Dependency in the Field
AI-assisted inspection tools route imagery to centralized cloud 
servers. In remote hangars, forward operating bases, and island 
airports — where MRO is most critical — bandwidth is limited or 
absent. Latency stretches from seconds to hours, grounding 
aircraft when every minute counts.
The Gap: No reliable, offline-capable AI system exists for real-time MRO defect detection independent of network infrastructure.

Objective & Approach
03
Objective: Build a fully offline, software-defined computer vision pipeline that detects aircraft surface defects in real-time on 
standard CPU hardware — with zero cloud or network dependency at any stage.
Edge-First Design
Inference runs entirely on a local 
CPU using ONNX Runtime. No 
cloud calls at any stage.
Optimized Model
YOLOv8n fine-tuned on industrial 
defect data, exported to INT8 
ONNX via Static PTQ for <30ms 
latency.
Explainability
Grad-CAM overlays show 
technicians exactly what drove 
each detection — not just a 
bounding box.
Full Workflow
From image capture to offline PDF 
maintenance report, the complete 
MRO workflow runs air-gapped.

Challenges Faced
06
CRITICAL
NEU Dataset Domain Gap
Challenge:
NEU dataset is flat steel imagery. Aircraft surfaces are curved, 
painted, and lit differently in hangars.
Mitigation:
Heavy Albumentations augmentation: perspective warps, CLAHE 
contrast shifts, synthetic crack overlays, hangar lighting simulation 
— applied before training.
CRITICAL
Grad-CAM / ONNX Incompatibility
Challenge:
Grad-CAM requires PyTorch autograd graph. ONNX Runtime 
decouples the model from PyTorch — Grad-CAM cannot run on 
ONNX models.
Mitigation:
Dual-model architecture: ONNX Runtime for primary inference. 
PyTorch .pt model retained separately, loaded on-demand for 
explainability, then unloaded to free RAM.
MODERATE
INT8 Quantization Accuracy Drop
Challenge:
Static PTQ can degrade small-object detection (hairline cracks, 
small fasteners) — the exact defects that matter most.
Mitigation:
Per-channel quantization (vs per-tensor). Decision matrix: drop 
<2% → ship; drop 2–4% → per-channel retry; drop >4% → 
escalate to QAT.
MODERATE
Heuristic Severity Triage
Challenge:
No learned severity classifier exists for this PoC scope. Rule-based 
triage on detection area × confidence is not aerospace-grade.
Mitigation:
Documented explicitly as a PoC-scope simplification. Production 
path: trained classifier head validated against ASME/SAE defect 
grading standards.

Technical Implementation
07
Training
PyTorch + Ultralytics YOLOv8
Transfer learning from COCO. 100-150 epochs, batch 16, 
img 640.
Augmentation
Albumentations
Perspective warp, CLAHE, brightness, synthetic crack 
overlay.
Export
ONNX
Framework-agnostic model format. Dynamic axes for 
flexible input.
Quantization
ONNX Runtime PTQ (INT8)
Static PTQ with CalibrationDataReader on 100 
augmented images. Per-channel.
Inference
ONNX Runtime (CPU Provider)
<30ms per frame. No GPU. InferenceSession + NMS 
post-processing.
Vision
OpenCV
Resize 640×640, normalize, CLAHE on grayscale channel.
Explainability
pytorch-grad-cam
On-demand. Last conv layer hook. Heatmap overlaid on 
source frame.
Dashboard
Streamlit
Local browser UI. st.cache_resource for model warmup.
Reports
fpdf2
Offline PDF. Header, annotated images, defect table, 
sign-off block.

Future Enhancements
10
OpenVINO Optimization
Export to Intel OpenVINO INT8 for x86 CPUs. 
Projected 40-50% further latency reduction over 
ONNX Runtime on Intel hardware.
Quantization-Aware Training
If Static PTQ accuracy drop exceeds threshold, 
retrain with simulated INT8 precision using QAT — 
forces the model to adapt to quantization during 
learning.
Real Aerospace Dataset
Supplement NEU with actual aerospace inspection 
imagery (fuselage, nacelle, wing surfaces) to fully 
close the domain gap from flat steel to curved 
aircraft surfaces.
Learned Severity Classifier
Replace heuristic area×confidence triage with a 
trained classifier head, validated against ASME/SAE 
defect grading standards for production-grade 
severity scoring.
Fleet-Level Aggregation
Extend to multi-aircraft defect tracking across a 
fleet. Detect systemic structural patterns across 
registration IDs over time.
Hardware Security Module
Integrate HSM-based authentication for report 
signing, ensuring tamper-proof maintenance 
records acceptable to airworthiness regulators.
